text:
morgan: Heads-up — seeing KV cache memory slowly climb on H100 during long streaming workloads. Pattern looks like a shadowpool -> evict oscillation when PCIe/backpressure spikes. repro bundle uploading.

sanjay: Can you drop the telemetry and a short repro? which kernels/path? :eyes:

morgan: quick paste of the hot lines from the bench run:
```
[2024-02-12 14:02:11] kvcache: alloc window=92345 used=0.85 free=7640
[2024-02-12 14:02:12] kvcache: evict enqueue id=0x7f3 thr=evict-1: queued
[2024-02-12 14:02:12] kvcache: pagewalk rate spike 4500/s -> 12000/s
[2024-02-12 14:02:13] shadowpool: refill failed, retrying; reuse-window shrink -> 2048
[2024-02-12 14:02:14] pager: fence wait delayed, compaction deferred
```
Looks like repeated enqueue -> failed reclaim -> reuse windows collapse -> more allocs.

elia: saw a similar oscillation on MI250 with the tiled kernels in paged-attn. Not seeing it on RTX6000 in our runs. Might be architecture timing / fence ordering.

pat: any obvious regression window? did this start after the batching heuristics change last week?

morgan: maybe related. The roll for continuous batching changed default tbatcher timeout and that increases steady inflight small requests. Repro fairly stable on commit c3a9b2.

pat: steps to repro for me to run?

morgan: quick repro (linux lab):
```
./bench/run_paged_attn --model=gpt-small --tokens=1_000_000 --batch=8 --streaming=1 \
  --kvcache.shadowpool=1 --tbatcher.mode=continuous --gpu=h100-1
```
Config snippet I used:
```
kvcache:
  shadowpool: true
  target_util: 0.85
  async_reclaim: true
bench:
  streaming: true
  batch_size: 8
```

perf-bot: Flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.redwood/fg/abcd1234 (heap + cpu for kvcache)

sanjay: thx. can you also run with rt_trace=1 and collect pagewalk counters? I'm wondering if the pagewalk walker is being scheduled twice under backpressure. try toggling TILE_SIZE kernel param (64 vs 128) too — kernel selection might change coalescing.

elia: quick patch that helped on MI250 for me (avoid double-queue):
```diff
--- a/runtime/kvcache/evict_queue.cpp
+++ b/runtime/kvcache/evict_queue.cpp
@@ -102,7 +102,8 @@
-  if (item->queued) return;
-  item->queued = true;
+  // avoid race where item is re-queued while previous evict job still pending
+  if (atomic_exchange(&item->queued, true)) return;
```
Small change — on MI250 it reduced spike frequency by ~70% in my runs.

morgan: interesting. On H100 I traced a delayed fence in the PCI DMA path: compaction completes but PTEs aren't recycled until the dma-fence is signaled much later; that keeps PTEs pinned causing allocs to grow.

pat: could be combined effect: kernel selection for tiled kernels produces different writeback ordering which interacts with fence signaling on different drivers.

sanjay: plan: (1) collect rt_trace/pagewalk counters from morgan run, (2) test elia's patch across H100 and A100, (3) toggle tbatcher timeout to previous value to see delta. assigning to eng-runtime triage.

morgan: uploading repro tarball and a quick script to reproduce. I'll flip the tbatcher timeout locally and re-run perf and rt_trace.

perf-bot: Trace artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1729991234/repro.tar.gz

elia: FYI I also reproduced on MI250 with batch=4 streaming but it didn't escalate to memory growth — just more frequent short-lived spikes. H100 profile shows persistent growth which suggests delayed reclaim path.

pat: let's sync 30min after runs. can someone post the minimal command to enable rt_trace collection? saves time.

sanjay: command:
```
sudo sysctl -w dev.kvcache.rt_trace=1
./bench/run_paged_attn --collect-rttrace --out=rttrace.json
```

morgan: running now. will report back with counters and timeline. tagging @elia @sanjay @pat for followup. :+1:

sanjay: adding a TODO to bugtriage: prioritize cross-arch repro + test candidate fix (atomic queue) + check fence handling in dma path.

pat: thanks — moving to triage board and creating a short-run on the infra bench fleet.

morgan: thanks team. I suspect this will be one of those multi-factor timing bugs (tbatcher + kernel selection + fence ordering). will post results.
